sources.name: Ember Yearly Electricity Data
sources.scope: Annual electricity generation and production-based full-lifecycle greenhouse-gas emissions. Ember reports nine fuel groups and national carbon intensity; its EU yearly generation is gross generation and its net-generation emissions factors are adjusted accordingly.
transformations: Filtered Area to Germany, France, and Poland and Year to 2018-2025.
Mapped country names to ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes.
Merged Total Generation (TWh), Total emissions (mtCO2), and source-reported CO2 intensity (gCO2/kWh) into one total row per country-year.
Merged generation (TWh) and emissions (mtCO2) for Ember's nine Fuel rows.
Derived fuel-row intensity as 1000 * emissions_mtco2e / generation_twh from the source's rounded values; left it blank where both generation and emissions are zero.
Assigned finalized to 2018-2024 and provisional to 2025 as artifact qualifications; these status values are not fields copied from the Ember download.
sources.qualification: The primary paper comparison uses only 2018-2024. The 2025 rows are supplementary because latest-year annual estimates can be assembled from monthly sources, including ENTSO-E for France and Poland, and are therefore not treated as fully independent evidence.

sources.name: EEA ENER038: Greenhouse gas emission intensity of electricity generation
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 (EEA materials unless otherwise indicated)
sources.scope: Annual greenhouse-gas emission intensity of gross electricity generation from main-activity producers and autoproducers. The series covers combustion-related CO2e, applies zero factors to nuclear and renewables, and does not include lifecycle upstream or construction emissions.
transformations: Parsed the source's semicolon-delimited wide table and selected Germany, France, and Poland.
Unpivoted calendar years 2018-2024 and mapped country names to ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 codes.
Removed thousands separators when parsing numeric values; no unit conversion or interpolation was applied.
Assigned finalized to 2018-2023 and early_estimate to 2024, following the EEA qualification of 2024 as an early estimate.
sources.qualification: EEA ENER038 is an orthogonal trend check rather than an interchangeable lifecycle benchmark because its accounting boundary differs from the study model and Ember.
